about: Paztport version 4 conformance vectors. Every case carries all of its inputs; keys and policies are named and defined in this file. Each key's private key is the PKCS#8 DER 302e020100300506032b657004220420 || seed, where seed = SHA-256(utf8("paztport-v3-vector-key:" + name)), and its public key is the SPKI DER export; both are base64url. Each policy is a Merkle tree of depth 8 whose routes fill the first leaves in the order its routes list them. Its rootId is "v" + the first 12 hex digits of SHA-256(utf8(its routes joined by newline)), each route's leaf salt is the first 16 bytes of SHA-256(utf8("paztport-v3-vector-salt:" + route)), and the leaf hash in each slot i after the routes, up to 2^depth − 1, is SHA-256(utf8("paztport-v3-vector-pad:" + rootId + ":" + i)), taken as it is, not hashed as a leaf; mesh-second, below, derives its rootId and salts with a seed as well. A handshake nonce labelled l is the first 16 bytes of SHA-256(utf8("paztport-v3-vector-nonce:" + l)), base64url: every request's nonce is labelled client, and every reply's server. The v3 in these seed strings is historical: version 3's vectors used them, and keeping them keeps every key and policy unchanged. This placement and rootId derivation are for the vectors only; real builds use random slots and a random rootId. Ed25519 is deterministic, so the file is reproduced byte for byte. The core sections use a made-up extension, example, name influence only as an opaque second name, and need no extension's rules. recordedLocalStep, responseAttestation, sessionParams, sessionResult, bindMcpCall and bindResult belong to the MCP profile. Of these only recordedLocalStep needs the influence extension's rules, since the client's local gate decides by them: a step's blocks carry influence entries, which the verifier reads (INFLUENCE_MISMATCH) and under whose classes it derives the gate's verdict again, by the owner-aware rule alone, since every stamp of a step is the client's own. Every other section that needs them is in the top-level member influence. blocks.read reads each token as blocks: expected is OK with the blocks read, or REFUSED; blocks.commit gives a block's JCS text and its stamp's ext. Each verify and offline case, each call of a recordedCall case, and each recordedLocalStep case's step, carries `blocksToken`, the token the verifier reads, null when no token was received, which is one empty block per stamp, and `blocks`, the token's readable value. `blocks` is null where there is no token, and in the two verify cases whose token does not read as an array: "a blocks token holding null, every ext empty", whose token is the JCS of null, and "a blocks token that does not read", whose token is not canonical bytes and has no readable value. The verify case "a block with a member blocks do not have" carries its readable value, an array whose second element is no block. On each verify, offline, recordedCall and responseAttestation case, `actsOn` is the extensions the verifier acts on, and `allowedExtensions` the names it carries, null for unset, which carries any name. A verify or offline case's expected is {reason, suspectSvc, suspectInst, handOver}: handOver is null unless the reason is OK, and then has one member per name in actsOn, each an array of {svc, items}, one per stamp in chain order, items null where the stamp's block does not name the extension. A verify case runs the live verifier `uses` times against one nonce cache of nonceTtlMs and expects the last result; each use is sent by `peer`, or, in a case with `peers` in place of `peer`, by peers[i] for use i (null: no peer). Its policyNotAfter is the earlier of the latest notAfter of the keyrings and the latest notAfter of the roots the verifier pins (one of each: the earlier of the two), which `now` must not pass. An offline case runs the offline verifier once: `recordedTs.last` is the recorded time of the last stamp, `rid` the record's rid, `prompt` the run's recorded prompt, and callMaxAgeMs and runMaxAgeMs the age limits; a null recordedTs is a record with no time, and a null limit is one not configured, which is absent, never 0; there is no peer, clock or nonce TTL, and `seen` is the set of nonce keys already spent in the record set. A policy's proof is looked up by `proofRoute` (null: no proof). A nonce key, in `nonceKey` and `seen`, is the JCS text of its array of strings, each string written as RFC 8785 writes strings. The verify case "a call id holding a noncharacter"'s nonceKey, and the responseAttestation case of that name's call.callId, hold the noncharacter U+FFFF written as itself, as json.json already does, which a strict reader refuses, so a replay reads this file's own structure with any JSON reader, and only the tokens with the reader under test. A sessionReply case is the client's check of `reply` at `now`, against `pin` and `serverEntry`, with the extensions it `requires` ([] when absent); offline the same reply opened an attested session exactly when the check gives ATTESTED or EXTENSION_REQUIRED, since step 5 is live only. A sessionRequirement case is what a client that requires the extensions `requires` may do after the handshake: `check` is the reply's check (null for a JSON-RPC error, Method not found among them, or a timeout), `listed` the reply's extensions ([] when it did not read) and `continueWithout` its switch; expected says whether it makes calls and the `requires` its calls carry. A sessionStatus case is the server's status for `request` at `now`, against its own `serverRoot` and `serverKeyring` (whose notAfter is its window), its policy key `serverPolicyKey` and the client policy keys `pinned`. A sessionRequest case is a request as received, its bytes in `requestToken`, read by the server: `expected` is OK for a well-formed request and MALFORMED for one it refuses (JSON-RPC -32602, HTTP 400 INVALID_PARAMS). A recordedLocalStep case is a recorded local step: its `step` (the call's `tool`, `callId` and `input`; the gate's decision, `resolved`, `verdict`, `routeAllowed` and `rulesHash`, recorded together as `decisionToken`; `rid`, `now`, the chain, `proofRoute`, and the blocks, unless the case's name says otherwise the origin's naming influence with [] and the hop's holding the session's entries), checked against its `client` (`keyring` by name, `policy`'s root, their windows `rootNotAfter` and `keyringNotAfter`, and `rules`), its `signers`, its `run` (prompt and start times) and `seen`; expected is the reason, and the verdict the step signed when it verifies, else null. A responseAttestation case is a response as the client receives it: `attestationToken` (its readable value `attestation`, one block per stamp of the response chain unless the case's name says otherwise), the `result` it answers, the `call` (`rid`, `callId`, `receiver`), the client's `actsOn` and `allowedExtensions`, and the `server` its stamps are checked against; the client checks it once at `now`, check 9c included, and expected is the reason, RID_MISMATCH for a call whose rid is not the first stamp's, before the chain is checked. The attestationToken of "an attestation whose members are not in JCS order" writes the members chain, proof, blocks, resultHash, out of JCS order; every other is its value's JCS. A sessionParams case is paztport/session's params as the server reads them (OK, or INVALID_PARAMS for JSON-RPC -32602), and a sessionResult case its result as the client reads it (OK, or MALFORMED_REPLY); the OK results carry the reply of the sessionReply case "entry-key form attested". The sections fixedInputs, deriveSessionId, bindPrompt, bindResponse, merkle, bindMcpCall and bindResult, which follow sessionRequest, pin the primitives the cases above rely on, each with its inputs: fixedInputs are `length` consecutive bytes from `start`, base64url, which deriveSessionId's cases name; the prompt and response bindings; merkle, a tree of its own (depth 8, rootId merkle-vector) whose leaf hashes, node, root, proofs and proof headers (the base64url of each proof's JCS bytes) are recorded as the library computes them, and whose padding hashes are recorded as given, not derived; and the MCP profile's tools/call and result bindings, bindMcpCall and bindResult. The member influence, last, holds: entries and labels, {name, item, reads}, whether the item reads as an entry on a request's block or as a label on a response's; rule, the owner-aware rule's truth table {name, influence, destinationOwner, refused}, with a null owner unknown; request, {name, stamps, served, write, destinationOwner, expected: {reason, everyStampNames}}, what an attested MCP server that acts on influence decides from the items handed on under influence: `stamps` holds them, one {svc, items} per stamp, items null where the block does not name influence (a pass-along block and an origin's among them), `served` is the classes the server served in the session and `write` whether the call writes to a public destination; `stamps` [] is nothing handed on (influence.md, What the rules read), where the every-stamp rule has no stamp to read and does not refuse, and everyStampNames is recorded true; an item that does not read as an entry is INFLUENCE_MISMATCH before any rule, and everyStampNames is then null; response, {name, reason, stamps, src, resultHash, expected: {entries}}, the entries a client that acts on influence adds for a response over MCP: the case hands the core check's result `reason` and `stamps`, what the response's blocks hold under influence, one per stamp, both to the implementation, which takes labels only when the reason is OK (for a result no check ran on, as in an unsafe session, `reason` is null, and `stamps` then null); and recordedCall, in recordedCall's shape, at a verifier that acts on influence and reads the items once the offline order gives OK, before a call is held to its session's limits. response, and the request cases whose `served` is not empty, record the MCP rule (every block of an MCP response chain names influence; the classes an MCP server served in its session), so they are for an implementation that acts on influence and implements the MCP profile; entries, labels, rule, recordedCall and the request cases whose `served` is [] are the extension's alone. A verify or offline case may pin several keyrings and roots: `keyrings` ([{keyring, notAfter}], in place of `keyring`) and `roots` ([{policy, notAfter}], which pin those policies' roots), where `policy` then names only where the case's proof comes from; in an offline case a member without a notAfter has no window. A case's one `keyring`, or `policy`'s root when it has no `roots`, is a single member whose window is the case's policyNotAfter in a verify case and none in an offline case, and two `roots` naming one policy are its root and a renewal of it. The policy mesh-second is a second tree over mesh's routes, whose rootId and salts the vectors derive from the seed `second` as well as the routes (rootId = "v" + first 12 hex of SHA-256(utf8(routes joined by newline + newline + "#second")), salt = the first 16 bytes of SHA-256(utf8("paztport-v3-vector-salt:second:" + route))); mesh-relabelled holds mesh's proofs with their rootId set to mesh-second's, over mesh's root. Cases may be added; a recorded answer changes only with a protocol change.
